text:
Jen (Support): Hey all — Escalation from a customer after yesterday's onboarding of the new LLM variant to hosted. They report a sharp p95/p99 regressions. p95 went from ~1.2s to ~3.7s for short prompts; p99 spikes to ~8–12s for long-context (>4096 token) calls. No auth/billing flags on their side. Sample request IDs: req_7a9, req_7b0, req_7c1. Can runtime/infra triage? :exclamation:

Mira (CS): Customer is DataAnalytics Inc — very sensitive to latency. They saw the regression right after we flipped the traffic to the new model pool. They already tried simple retries and small payload throttling, no change. They're asking for temporary mitigation (route to previous model or rollback).

Alex (Runtime): I'm pulling traces now. Initial glance at traces shows a lot of tail time spent in KV cache compaction and tokenization step for requests >2k tokens. Interesting bit: a bunch of requests show many small kernel launches on GPU (inefficient batching). Could be a change in how the new model's tokenizer divides long inputs.

Li (Infra): Checking infra metrics — GPU utilization is fine overall, but per-instance CUDA context switches up ~3x on the new pool. Network queues not saturated. I also see more CPU-side time in the worker (thread-blocking) when processing long contexts — maybe tokenizer CPU-bound.

Sam (Eng): Possible causes: 1) tokenizer updated to new BPE merge table that increases token counts for some inputs (=> longer sequences). 2) new model has attention patterns that trigger different kernel selection, hitting a slower path for certain seq lengths. 3) KV cache code path regression after optimizing for short-context throughput.

Jen (Support): Customer asked for repro steps. We need a concise reproduction: short prompt (<=256 tokens) and a long prompt (~6k tokens) that shows divergence. I attached a sanitized long prompt (same file across tickets).

Alex (Runtime): Repro I've been running (locally using their payload):
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "new-llm-2026-03",
  "input": "<6k-token-sanitized-payload>",
  "stream": false
}
```
p95 local: 3.4s, p99: 9.6s. If I switch model param to `new-llm-2026-03-quant` (smaller kernels) p95 improves to 1.5s.

Alex (Runtime): Also tried swapping tokenizer to the old merge table while keeping the new model weights; p95 drops to ~1.2s. So evidence points at the tokenizer producing longer tokenized lengths for the same text.

Li (Infra): Quick mitigation options: 1) Route affected customer back to the previous model pool (fast rollback). 2) Configure request-level model fallback for that route to `stable-llm-2025` until we fix. Both are doable now. 3) Short-term: enable larger batching on the new pool to amortize kernel launch overhead, but that may add latency for short requests.

Mira (CS): Customer prefers rollback to previous model pool. Please advise ETA. They need the SLA preserved.

Sam (Eng): Root-cause plan: we'll (A) confirm tokenizer diffs (merge tables + byte-level mapping), (B) profile kernel selection for representative seq lengths especially 2048/4096/6144, (C) add guardrail so kernel fallback prefers the low-latency path for common seq lengths.

Alex (Runtime): Immediate action: I can add a route-level override to send DataAnalytics traffic to `stable-llm-2025` now. That requires a config push and a quick smoke test. I'll do it and report back in ~10m.

oncall-bot: Automated note — creating incident stub INC-2026-324 for latency regression (severity: high).

Jen (Support): Thanks. Alex pls confirm once rollback is live. Also capture the exact sample request IDs so CS can close the loop.

Alex (Runtime): Rolled back their route traffic to `stable-llm-2025` and warmed a warm worker pool. Per telemetry: p95 reported to customer dropped back to ~1.1s within two minutes. I pushed config-change-987. Smoke tests: `req_7a9` now 1.0s, `req_7b0` 1.2s, `req_7c1` 1.1s.

Mira (CS): Shared update with customer — they're happy with rollback for now but asked for a post-mortem and timeline for a proper fix.

Sam (Eng): Next steps: Eng to reproduce locally with tokenization diff patch and generate a minimal failing test. Priority: blocker for the onboard. Can someone export tokenizer mapping diffs for the sanitized payload?

Alex (Runtime): I exported the token counts for the same payload across versions:
- stable-llm-2025 tokenizer: 4,512 tokens
- new-llm-2026 tokenizer: 6,128 tokens
That's a ~35% token count increase — explains the kernel path flip and KVCACHE churn.

Li (Infra): Filing infra action items: 1) Add monitoring alert to detect sudden per-request token count increases by model version. 2) Add quick rollback runbook link to the incident page.

Jen (Support): I'll keep the customer updated and schedule a follow-up meeting for Friday with engineering. Please add a short blameless summary in the incident.

Sam (Eng): For the dev fix: either revert tokenizer merge table or implement token-length-aware kernel heuristics. We'll try a patch that normalizes the tokenization for certain unicode sequences where we saw the biggest delta. Timeline: PR in 24h, bench in 48h, staged rollout with A/B in 72h if all green.

Alex (Runtime): One more note — the new model had an aggresssive KV cache eviction policy change (default TTL smaller) which amplified the problem for long-context chats: more cache misses = more recompute. I'm reverting that config on the new pool while we fix tokenizer. That should reduce tail.

Mira (CS): Customer requested an ETA for final fix. I'll give them the 72h window but will emphasize we will coordinate on the staged rollout.

Jen (Support): Great — thanks everyone. I'll update the incident and mark this thread as active until post-mortem is posted.

Li (Infra): Logging action items to INC-2026-324: add token-count alert, rollback runbook, temp config revert of KV TTL, and add test to CI that compares token counts for onboarding models.

Sam (Eng): Will follow up with a short write-up in the incident with reproduction steps, diffs, and perf numbers.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-324 updated: status -> mitigated (customer rerouted).

Jen (Support): Closing loop here — customer confirmed latency stabilized after rollback. Leaving this thread open till post-mortem. :thumbsup:
